html:
Mexican painter famous for her intense self-portraits and her pride in Mexican culture. She was born in Coyoacán, now part of Mexico City, in the family home known as the Blue House, where she also died.

She had polio as a child. At eighteen a bus she was riding was hit by a tram, leaving her with terrible injuries and pain for the rest of her life. She began painting in bed, using a mirror fixed above her.

In 1929 she married the muralist Diego Rivera, a leader of Mexican muralism; they divorced and remarried. Both were communists, and in 1937 they took in the exiled Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky.

Her paintings show her body, her pain, her marriage and her mixed Mexican and European roots, as in The Two Fridas (1939). She wore Tehuana dress and drew on folk art, part of the national pride that followed the Mexican Revolution. The surrealists claimed her, but she said she painted her own reality, not dreams. Since the 1980s she has become one of the best-known artists in the world.
